videos.script: Panela has nearly five thousand customers who ordered in the last year. Sending all of them the same email is the easiest thing to do, and one of the least useful. {{same}} A customer who ordered yesterday and a customer who has not ordered since the winter need different messages. So does a customer who orders every week, and one who ordered twice. {{different}} Segmentation puts customers into a handful of groups that can each be treated one way. {{segments}} RFM is the oldest method and still the most used. Three questions about each customer. How recently did they order? How often? How much? Score each one from one to five, and the scores name the groups. {{rfm}} Clustering is the other way. Give an algorithm the same three numbers and let it find the groups itself. {{cluster}} Both give groups. Neither says the groups are right. That depends on whether a team can do something different for each one. {{useful}} This lesson builds both for Panela, and compares what they find. {{end}}
